doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Growing up in Pensacola: bands and early jazz
summary: Born in Mariana, Florida, Billie was raised in Pensacola and recalls the Douglas and Joe Jesse orchestras, the instrumentation and jazz there.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Where were you born, Billy?
Well, I was born in Mariana, Florida.
Whereabouts is that?
That's between Pensacola and Jacksonville, Florida. Between those two towns.
How long did you stay in Mariana?

How long I stayed in Mariana, I guess. I stayed in Mariana. When my mother moved out of Mariana, I was quite a baby. We moved into Pensacola, Florida. So I raised in Pensacola, but I wasn't born there.
What kind of music did you hear around Pensacola when you were going around as a young girl?
Nothing but the, what you call the, ragtime music. Or ragtime music like that, you know. Jazz.
Would they have the bands?
Well, sure.
They had bands over there.
Yeah, sure.
Do you remember any of the outstanding bands there?
Yeah. Yeah. Douglas Orchestra. And Joe Jesse Orchestra. That's when during that time. Stay there.
What about Douglas' full name? Do you remember that?
George.
George Douglas. Uh-huh.
Over there, there were quite a few bands there.
Do you remember what the lineup in those bands would be?
Well, they had trumpet, trombone, banjo, drum, piano, and bass.
Pretty much like the New Orleans.
Yeah, same thing as New Orleans jazz. They're all the same thing.
Have good clarinet players over there? Do you remember any of them?

Well, let me see. Well, uh... What do you find a player? Let's see. Well, yeah, uh... Let's see now I'm calling it. Well, uh... The Douglas... The brothers... The brothers of them had a band. You know what I mean? You know? They played, uh... Trombone. Banjo. You know? Trombone. And, uh... Trombone. I mean, clannet. They had clannet in that time. You know, they was playing then.
George Douglas played which instrument?
He played trombone.
Do you remember the names of the other brothers?
I can't remember the other names of his brothers.
Do you remember the names of any of the other men over there on the different instruments?
Well, uh... Clounce... Clounce... Nelson... He was one of the greatest violin... Jazz violin that, uh... In that time... You know... Play. And he was really a jazz violin player.
And where was he from?
Tonsacola.
When did jazz start over there? Do you remember?
Well... Jazz... I'm telling you... Since I've been big enough to know what music was... It was jazz then.
They had jazz going on in Pensacola?
Yeah. Yeah, they had jazz then.
